findings.title: Recited speech reaches the speaking jaw
findings.claim: As exploratory attributed wordplay, commanded speech and later recitation reach the jaw/chin that becomes the point of bodily yielding.
findings.mechanism: The saying carrier opens the focus, recitation supplies sound following sound, and collapse ends at the jaw junction; together they turn the speaking body's hinge into the endpoint of prostration.
findings.reader_payoff: The chin can be perceived as more than an endpoint: it is also the bodily hinge associated with speech that begins and travels through the ayah.
findings.containment: This is embodied wordplay only; it does not make chin a lexical meaning of speech or replace the chin as the fall's endpoint.
